Too much RPG voice acting just feels like "Look ma, I'm reading lines!" Adds almost nothing to the product. In fact, a lot of times the dialog is so merely adequate, trying to act it out just breaks whatever fragile suspension of disbelief you were maintaining.
And Irenicus was voiced by David Warner, a stage, TV, film, and voice actor who'd been in the business for 30+ years at the time of BG2.

I've been playing Torment: Tides of Numenera. 1% of dialogue is voiced. For that type of game, more voice acting would be prohibitively expensive and limit writing changes during development. The game being mostly an interactive novel, that'd be a death sentence.

In the future, we'll have text-to-speech which is 99% indistinguishable from human speech. Then voice artists will sell licences for their voices and we'll have the best of both worlds.

https://youtu.be/4kSGkGKwp9U

Watch that video about specifically why Anthony Hopkins' acting was so great in Westworld. Even if text to speech is getting better at not being blatantly artificial, it's going to have a long ways to go before it can act.

I don't think it's as far off as you might believe. Just look at graphics and how fast that progressed. Artists and animators are responsible for a lot of what we see in games. Even when someone is motion captured their performance is often tweaked in post production. Having someone who can act at this point is less important than having someone who understands acting and has the technical knowledge to use the digital art tools.

I donno. I'll believe it when I hear it. I think it's at least 10 years off, but if I were being super optimistic I might say 5 until it's at least better than the B-list (or C or D-list) actors they have doing video games now. But I sincerely doubt they'll ever match the artistry real A-list actors can bring to their voice work (when they are on point).

You mentioned CG faces and mocap, but even when I see CG faces doing emotions, the transitions are usually too harsh and unnatural. They come off schizophrenic or bipolar. Watch that video again and see how smooth and subtly Anthony Hopkins can move from one emotion to another.

The thing is, when CG is done properly you don't even know it's there. When it's done badly, it's all you see. CG is used in virtually every modern movie now and it's not always so easy to pick out in a lot of cases. A great example is how they brought back Peter Cushing as Tarkin in Rogue One even though he's now dead. Another example is the hit show The Expanse (if you haven't touched this one yet, do it - you owe it to yourself) which makes heavy use of an extremely well done practical effects and CG mashup. The progress that has been made on the CG front in the last 25 years is nothing short of astonishing.

I think when they finally nail voice synthesis (we're not there yet) it'll be the same. They'll use it all over the place, and you won't even realize they're doing it.
Note the type of games I talked about. Voice synthesis is unlikely to replace the main story line cutscenes in your witcher 3.

Interesting that you bring up voice synthesis.

With the current state of voice synthesis, is it worth including lip-synced voice synthesis in what would otherwise be text only dialog?

Depends on what counts as "current".
Adobe showed some crazy tech recently, but it's unclear how it handles inflection.
no. one of my problems with RPG games in general is that conversations take way too long even when all you're doing is clicking the button to skip the convo without reading it.

Personally, think Dragon Age Origins nailed it best. Everyone but your character was voiced so you ended up reading the lines out loud anyway to yourself, immersing you further. You always knew what you were going say in a situation (none of this vague option shit from Fallout 4/Mass Effect) and there were still plenty of options.

No voice acting unless it is Japanese and not too much branching. I don't want to play ten million times to see all dialogue. If voice acting is added, it better not have great long pauses in the middle (I'm looking at you Hyperdimension Neptunia).
